resolution_policy: Resolve each declaration through method_id/context_id/owner_id; source-unit views may apply explicit declaration_variants. These references preserve every retained condition, object, proof method and provenance value. Private and notation entries are historical source identities, not independent claims of current kernel verification.

complete_v4_catalog.contains: Full original proof/source excerpts, module docstrings and all pre-normalization metadata.

archives.link_replacement: Repeated source_unit_id/source_unit_ids fields are represented by central source-unit IDs, per-module declaration_ids and explicit source-unit views.

frozen_sources_and_booklets.contains: Frozen source booklets, inspected source preimages, exact proof extraction and replacement receipts; original /tmp paths resolve as tar members after removing /tmp/.

archives.publication_note: Historical preimages and frozen-booklet artifacts are retained in the private local development backup. development-archive:// locators preserve historical identity, not files shipped in this release. m-466f6fcad322f429043a7daf.proof_detail: Declaration intent: **Differentiability of a concave pressure from interval slopes.** If `p` is concave near zero and, along a sequence `t n > 0` tending to zero, the interval slopes over `[t n, 2 t n]` and `[-2 t n, -t n]` share a limit `d`, then `p` is differentiable at zero with derivative `d`. metadata_inheritance.module_objects: blockFinset: fiber of a finite block-label map; blockMatchSize: min(source block size, target block size); sourceBlockSubset,targetBlockSubset: chosen subsets of their original block fibers, both of cardinality blockMatchSize; residualSource,residualTarget: complements of the selected within-block endpoints; their cardinalities agree; blockEquiv,residualEquiv: finite-set bijections used to select actual edges; blockMatching: full cardinality N matching assembled from within-block edges and residual edges; B: a pointwise real upper bound on residual edge costs
metadata_inheritance.module_proof_detail: Partition each cloud by label, choose equally many source and target endpoints in each block, and prove all chosen blocks disjoint. Use finite cardinality equality to construct a bijection in each selected block and a bijection of the remaining endpoints. Combine the disjoint graphs, prove row/column injectivity by membership in unique block fibers or their complements, and count the edges. Split the finite cost sum over the disjoint block and residual graphs; bound every residual summand by B and compare the full matching with the infimum.

    {X : Type*} {K : ℕ} {C : ℕ → Type*}
    [∀ k, Fintype (C k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (C k)]
    (cell : (k : ℕ) → X → C k)
    (hnested : ∀ (k l : ℕ), k ≤ l → ∀ u v : X,

    {a b : ℕ} (x : Fin a → X) (y : Fin b → X)
    (cost : Fin a → Fin b → ℝ)
    (σ0 : PartialMatching a b)
    (hleaf : ∀ e ∈ σ0.edges, cell K (x e.1) = cell K (y e.2))
    (hmax : ∀ c : C K,
      (σ0.edges.filter (fun e => cell K (x e.1) = c)).card =
        min ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i => cell K (x i) = c)).card)
            ((Finset.univ.filter (fun j => cell K (y j) = c)).card))
    (B : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hB : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < K → ∀ i j,
      cell k (x i) = cell k (y j) → cost i j ≤ B (k + 1))

      σ.card = min a b ∧
      σ.cost cost ≤ σ0.cost cost +
        ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (K + 1), if 0 < k then
          B k * (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
            ((∑ c : C k,
                |partitionCount (cell k ∘ x) c - partitionCount (cell k ∘ y) c|) -

    {σ : W → E} {B : Set W} {x₀ : E} {K : Set E} {ψ : E → ℝ}
    {T : ℝ × E → E} {r τ : ℝ} {C : ℝ≥0}
    (hB : IsOpen B) (h0 : (0 : W) ∈ B) (hσ : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 σ B)
    (hσ0 : σ 0 = x₀) (hinj : InjOn σ B) (hK : IsClosed K) (hr : 0 < r)
    (hT : LipschitzOnWith C T (Icc (-τ) τ ×ˢ closedBall x₀ r))
    (hfixed : ∀ t ∈ Icc (-τ) τ, InjOn (fun x ↦ T (t, x)) (closedBall x₀ r))
    (hclock : ∀ t ∈ Icc (-τ) τ, ∀ x ∈ K ∩ closedBall x₀ r,
      ψ (T (t, x)) = ψ x + t)
    (hlevel : ∀ w ∈ B, σ w ∈ K → ψ (σ w) = ψ x₀)

∃ a : ℝ, ∃ L : ℝ≥0, 0 < a ∧ ball 0 a ⊆ B ∧

      LipschitzOnWith L (fun q : ℝ × W ↦ T (q.1, σ q.2))
        (Ioo (-τ) τ ×ˢ ball 0 a) ∧
      (∀ q ∈ Ioo (-τ) τ ×ˢ (ball 0 a ∩ σ ⁻¹' K),
        ψ (T (q.1, σ q.2)) = ψ x₀ + q.1) ∧
      InjOn (fun q : ℝ × W ↦ T (q.1, σ q.2))
        (Ioo (-τ) τ ×ˢ (ball 0 a ∩ σ ⁻¹' K)) ∧
      MeasurableSet (Ioo (-τ) τ ×ˢ (ball 0 a ∩ σ ⁻¹' K)) ∧

            dist l ((extChartAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) (old i)).symm x) = δ i ∧
            u ((extChartAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) (old i)).symm x) - u l = δ i ∧
            dist ((extChartAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) (old i)).symm x) r = δ i ∧

      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ P) x = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x ∧
      HasFDerivAt (fun y ↦ localHamiltonian (F.chartEnergy initial) e (y, fderiv ℝ P y))
        (0 : E →L[ℝ] ℝ) x ∧
      let n : E → E →L[ℝ] ℝ := fun y ↦
        (Real.sqrt (2 * localHamiltonian (F.chartEnergy initial) e (y, fderiv ℝ P y)))⁻¹ •
          fderiv ℝ P y
      n x = f' x ∧ HasFDerivAt n B x ∧ ContDiffAt ℝ ∞ n x ∧
      ∃ (U : Set (E × (E →L[ℝ] ℝ))) (Γ : (E × (E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) → ℝ → M),
        IsOpen U ∧ (x, f' x) ∈ U ∧
        (∀ q ∈ U, F.IsEulerLagrangeOn (Γ q) univ) ∧
        (∀ q ∈ U, F.chartMomentumFamily initial Γ (q, t₀) = q) ∧
        ∀ (σ : V → E) (offset₁ offset₂ : V → ℝ) (S : Set V) (w : V)
          (J : V →L[ℝ] E) (a : V →L[ℝ] ℝ),
          σ w = x → HasFDerivWithinAt σ J S w →
          HasFDerivWithinAt offset₁ a S w → HasFDerivWithinAt offset₂ a S w →
          offset₁ w = offset₂ w → ∀ (old : M) (r : ℝ),
          Γ (σ w, f' (σ w)) (r - offset₁ w) ∈ (extChartAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) old).source →
          ∃ L : V →L[ℝ] E × (E →L[ℝ] ℝ),
            F.chartMomentumFamily old Γ ((σ w, f' (σ w)), r - offset₁ w) =
              F.chartMomentumFamily old Γ ((σ w, n (σ w)), r - offset₂ w) ∧
            HasFDerivWithinAt
              (fun v ↦ F.chartMomentumFamily old Γ ((σ v, f' (σ v)), r - offset₁ v))
              L S w ∧
            HasFDerivWithinAt
              (fun v ↦ F.chartMomentumFamily old Γ ((σ v, n (σ v)), r - offset₂ v))
              L S w

**Per-sample Bennett-Bernstein MGF bound.** For a centred bounded measurable real random variable `Y` with `|Y| ≤ 2M`, mean zero, and centred moment bound `|E Y^k| ≤ σ² (2M)^{k-2}` for `k ≥ 2`, and any `0 ≤ t` with `2 M t < 1`, the moment generating function satisfies `mgf Y μ t ≤ exp(σ² t² / (2 (1 - 2 M t)))`. This is the per-sample MGF bound at the heart of vdV Lem 19.32. The proof is standard real analysis: `mgf_bounded_taylor` expands `mgf Y μ t` as a power series in `t`; the `k=0` term is `1`, the `k=1` term is `t · 0 = 0`, and the `k ≥ 2` tail is bounded by `∑_{k≥2} σ² (2Mt)^{k-2} t² / k! ≤ σ² t² · (1/2) · ∑_{j≥0} (2Mt)^j = σ² t² / (2 (1 - 2Mt))`, after which `1 + u ≤ exp u` upgrades the additive bound to the multiplicative form. The proof splits the Taylor series at indices `0`, `1` and the `k ≥ 2` tail, bounds the tail term-by-term by `σ² t² · (2Mt)^j / 2` (using `(j+2)! ≥ 2` and `hY_mom`), sums the geometric series via `tsum_geometric_of_lt_one`, and upgrades the additive bound `mgf ≤ 1 + ...` to the multiplicative form via `Real.add_one_le_exp`. Exact declared target/object: ProbabilityTheory.mgf Y μ t
      ≤ Real.exp (σ ^ 2 * t ^ 2 / (2 * (1 - 2 * M * t)))

Right-tail of the empirical process under iid bounded `f`: `μ {ω | x < G_n f (ω)} ≤ exp(-x²/(4(σ² + xM/√n)))`. Proof outline (vdV §19.6): * Express `G_n f (ω) = (1/√n) Σᵢ Y_i(ω)` where `Y_i(ω) = f(X_i ω) - Pf`. * Markov on the MGF `μ(G_n f > x) ≤ exp(-λ x) · μ[exp(λ G_n f)]` for any `λ > 0`. * iid factorisation via `iIndepFun.mgf_sum`: `μ[exp(λ G_n f)] = (μ[exp((λ/√n) Y_1)])^n`. * Power-series expansion (`mgf_bounded_taylor`): `μ[exp((λ/√n) Y_1)] = 1 + (1/n) · Σ_{k≥2} (λ/√n)^k/k! · P(f-Pf)^k` (the k=1 term vanishes since `P(f-Pf) = 0`). * Centered-moment bound (`centered_moment_bound_pow`): for `k ≥ 2`, `|P(f-Pf)^k| ≤ σ² · (2M)^{k-2}`. * Optimal-λ choice: `λ = (x/2) / (σ² + x M / √n)`. Telescoping the geometric series and using `(1 + a/n)^n ≤ exp(a)` gives `μ[exp(λ G_n f)] ≤ exp(λ x / 2)`. * Combine: `μ(G_n f > x) ≤ exp(-λ x + λ x / 2) = exp(-λ x / 2) = exp(-x²/(4(σ² + xM/√n)))`.     {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) (bands : Finset ι)

    (hgood : ∀ i ∈ bands, MemLp (((Small i)ᶜ ∪ Bad i)ᶜ.indicator (T i)) 2 P)

    {E C s H B c K : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hC : 0 ≤ C) (hB : 0 ≤ B)

    (hV : (∑ i ∈ bands, v i) ≤ E)
    (hmean : ∀ i ∈ bands,
      (∫ x, (((Small i)ᶜ ∪ Bad i)ᶜ.indicator (T i) x) ^ 2 ∂P) ≤ C * s ^ 2 * v i)
    (hbadNorm : ∀ i ∈ bands,

m-5693834b9156dd42e3691e7b.conditions: A uniformly continuous curve into a complete metric space, or a C1 Finsler curve whose actual speed is bounded; completeness is for that same Finsler length metric.
m-5693834b9156dd42e3691e7b.relation_to_sources: Exact interval specialization of the uniform extension theorem, combined with the Finsler length formula. It does not claim convergence of velocity or momentum.
m-5693834b9156dd42e3691e7b.objects: A speed-integral bound, Lipschitz control in the induced distance, and a continuous position extension from (a,b) to [a,b].
m-5693834b9156dd42e3691e7b.proof_detail: Integrate the constant speed bound; compare distance with subsegment length; obtain uniform continuity and extend Cauchy limits to the interval endpoints.

m-f32aea1606ddb1026d25a59f.conditions: A complete original length metric on a finite-dimensional Hausdorff preconnected smooth strongly convex Finsler manifold; one actual local nonzero-velocity solution.
m-f32aea1606ddb1026d25a59f.relation_to_sources: Manifold synthesis of unique maximal-solution construction with the locally proved complete-Finsler continuation criterion.
m-f32aea1606ddb1026d25a59f.objects: A global intrinsic Euler–Lagrange curve agreeing with the given local germ and initial tangent.
m-f32aea1606ddb1026d25a59f.proof_detail: Take the supremum of symmetric existence radii. Glue at a finite supremum and extend through both endpoints to contradict maximality; unbounded radii cover the real line.
m-f32aea1606ddb1026d25a59f.source_relation: Manifold synthesis of unique maximal-solution construction with the locally proved complete-Finsler continuation criterion.
m-f32aea1606ddb1026d25a59f.adaptation: Manifold synthesis of unique maximal-solution construction with the locally proved complete-Finsler continuation criterion.

m-dd48f46c2bebb3515c44c325.conditions: Locally unique intrinsic Finsler solutions on intervals all containing the same initial time, with equal actual initial tangent; an open target time set covered by those intervals.
m-dd48f46c2bebb3515c44c325.relation_to_sources: Intrinsic implementation of the overlap-gluing construction preceding the maximal-solution theorem.
m-dd48f46c2bebb3515c44c325.objects: One actual manifold-valued solution on the union, preserving the initial tangent.
m-dd48f46c2bebb3515c44c325.proof_detail: Connected-interval uniqueness makes chosen local representatives agree on every overlap. Choose a representative at each time and use local agreement to verify the equation and tangent.
m-dd48f46c2bebb3515c44c325.source_relation: Intrinsic implementation of the overlap-gluing construction preceding the maximal-solution theorem.
m-dd48f46c2bebb3515c44c325.adaptation: Intrinsic implementation of the overlap-gluing construction preceding the maximal-solution theorem.

m-de3972f025ad87ef4d888ee0.conditions: A continuous closed-interval curve for the compact left endpoint trace; for differential continuation, smooth strongly convex finite-dimensional Finsler data and compact coordinate confinement; original metric completeness for intrinsic continuation.
m-de3972f025ad87ef4d888ee0.relation_to_sources: Left-endpoint version of the same continuation synthesis. Teschl explicitly includes the left endpoint; the manifold chart and nonzero phase control are local formal developments.
m-de3972f025ad87ef4d888ee0.objects: A compact initial chart trace, a left chartwise ODE extension and an intrinsic extension to (a-delta,b).
m-de3972f025ad87ef4d888ee0.proof_detail: Construct the left endpoint chart trace; confine fixed positive speed phase; use the left-endpoint ODE continuation result; transfer back and glue.
m-de3972f025ad87ef4d888ee0.source_relation: Left-endpoint version of the same continuation synthesis. Teschl explicitly includes the left endpoint; the manifold chart and nonzero phase control are local formal developments.

m-bc4af8d85ea73202387fb66a.conditions: Smooth strongly convex Finsler energy at a nonzero chart phase.
m-bc4af8d85ea73202387fb66a.relation_to_sources: The source supplies the standard regular geodesic/EL ODE. The chart-domain and tangent-bundle data are explicit formal constructors rather than an assumed geodesic existence oracle.
m-bc4af8d85ea73202387fb66a.objects: A smooth local Euler–Lagrange curve with prescribed position and velocity, first in coordinates and then on the manifold.
m-bc4af8d85ea73202387fb66a.proof_detail: Construct a local Hamiltonian integral curve, invert Legendre coordinates, and identify its velocity and Euler–Lagrange momentum equation.
m-bc4af8d85ea73202387fb66a.adaptation: The source supplies the standard regular geodesic/EL ODE. The chart-domain and tangent-bundle data are explicit formal constructors rather than an assumed geodesic existence oracle.

m-e4f136724e8ab4053753275c.conditions: Two local chart EL curves with the same actual manifold tangent initial data, in possibly different charts.
m-e4f136724e8ab4053753275c.relation_to_sources: The cross-chart germ formulation is a derived manifold adapter to the standard ODE uniqueness theorem.
m-e4f136724e8ab4053753275c.objects: Coordinate and manifold equality on a neighborhood of the initial time.
m-e4f136724e8ab4053753275c.proof_detail: Choose a common overlap, rechart one solution, identify initial chart velocity and use Hamiltonian local uniqueness.
m-e4f136724e8ab4053753275c.adaptation: The cross-chart germ formulation is a derived manifold adapter to the standard ODE uniqueness theorem.

m-2e8060464a64864a6c18d96d.conditions: A C2 coordinate EL solution in the slit domain of a smooth strongly convex Finsler energy.
m-2e8060464a64864a6c18d96d.relation_to_sources: This is smooth ODE regularity applied to a regular Lagrangian; the hypothesis is C2, not already a smooth solution.
m-2e8060464a64864a6c18d96d.proof_detail: Lift to the smooth Hamiltonian ODE, bootstrap integral-curve regularity, and project back through the smooth inverse.
m-2e8060464a64864a6c18d96d.adaptation: This is smooth ODE regularity applied to a regular Lagrangian; the hypothesis is C2, not already a smooth solution.

m-3a09ff3d4d309db79bb7d1cc.conditions: A smooth energy with positive-definite fiber Hessian on an open finite-dimensional phase domain; two smooth EL curves have the same initial position and velocity.
m-3a09ff3d4d309db79bb7d1cc.relation_to_sources: A derived local regular-Lagrangian theorem; strong convexity supplies the invertible fiber Hessian. The statement constructs its inverse rather than assuming a preexisting Hamiltonian flow.
m-3a09ff3d4d309db79bb7d1cc.objects: The phase lift into position/covector space and uniqueness of its germ.
m-3a09ff3d4d309db79bb7d1cc.proof_detail: Construct the local Legendre inverse, lift both curves to one Hamiltonian vector field, and apply local ODE uniqueness.
m-3a09ff3d4d309db79bb7d1cc.adaptation: A derived local regular-Lagrangian theorem; strong convexity supplies the invertible fiber Hessian. The statement constructs its inverse rather than assuming a preexisting Hamiltonian flow.

m-796a6ba62aca0ae0e0ff7949.conditions: X is a metric space and base is an arbitrary point. The code stores one finite multiset in each half-open integer distance shell. The inverse equivalence from arbitrary locally finitely supported natural-valued functions additionally requires ProperSpace X. Shell measurability uses a Borel measurable structure; the configuration standard-Borel claim additionally uses StandardBorelSpace X.
m-796a6ba62aca0ae0e0ff7949.relation_to_sources: The distance-shell product is a concrete representation of locally finite counting measures with multiplicities. Its shell origin and code are implementation choices; no topology or Poisson law is imposed by the representation.
m-796a6ba62aca0ae0e0ff7949.objects: shellIndex: natural floor of dist(x,base); Shell base n: points with n <= dist(x,base) < n+1; LocalConfiguration base: the countable product of finite multisets on those disjoint shells; multiplicity: the count of x in its unique shell; windowSupport: the finite occupied support in shells with index below N; toLocallyFinsupp,ofLocallyFinsupp: decode/encode actual natural-valued locally finitely supported functions
m-796a6ba62aca0ae0e0ff7949.proof_detail: Use natural-floor inequalities for the unique shell and its Borel measurability. Take the finite union of supports of the first N shell multisets to control a ball. Decode multiplicities and use multiset extensionality for injectivity. For the converse, properness makes closed bounded shells compact; local finiteness then gives a finite support on each shell. Transfer standard-Borel structure through countable products of standard-Borel multiset shell spaces.
m-796a6ba62aca0ae0e0ff7949.adaptation: The distance-shell product is a concrete representation of locally finite counting measures with multiplicities. Its shell origin and code are implementation choices; no topology or Poisson law is imposed by the representation.

m-7b5e2ed99e29c44bbaeeebf6.conditions: X is a measurable standard-Borel point space with the library sorted-code multiset measurable structure. Measurability of Multiset.map f additionally requires a measurable standard-Borel target Y and measurable f. For sums, Y may instead be any additively commutative monoid with a measurable space and measurable binary addition. The parameterized sum permits any measurable parameter space A and a jointly measurable observable f : A x X -> Y.
m-7b5e2ed99e29c44bbaeeebf6.relation_to_sources: The canonical enumeration is a standard-Borel coding choice. Mapping and finite sums are measurable algebraic consequences; arbitrary measurable additive-monoid targets and external parameters generalize the real-valued counting-integral formula.
m-7b5e2ed99e29c44bbaeeebf6.objects: toFinitePointCloud: canonical measurable enumeration of a multiset by its chosen real coding order; codeSum: finite fold of an observable over the padded finite code; Multiset.map: pushforward of every atom, retaining its multiplicity; sum_map_param: sum of a jointly measurable point observable while preserving an external parameter
m-7b5e2ed99e29c44bbaeeebf6.proof_detail: Read the already-sorted multiset code as a finite ordered cloud. Use the cloud padded-code measurability and the exact order-forgetting inverse. Factor multiset pushforward through canonical enumeration, cloud mapping and measurable order-forgetting. Express sums as a finite option-code sum, split over the natural length, and use measurability of finite sums and addition; retain the parameter in the product carrier.
m-7b5e2ed99e29c44bbaeeebf6.adaptation: The canonical enumeration is a standard-Borel coding choice. Mapping and finite sums are measurable algebraic consequences; arbitrary measurable additive-monoid targets and external parameters generalize the real-valued counting-integral formula.

m-14787af7903ed13a532f6228.conditions: X is metric and config is a shell configuration at an arbitrary base. N and M are natural integer window radii; the nested-window identity assumes M <= N. The algebraic observable-sum formula works for any additive commutative monoid Y. Measurable window sums additionally require X Borel and standard Borel, Y measurable with measurable addition, and a measurable point observable.
m-14787af7903ed13a532f6228.relation_to_sources: Integer open-ball restriction and finite shell sums implement bounded-window counting. Measurability follows from the code; continuity across a hard shell boundary is not asserted.
m-14787af7903ed13a532f6228.objects: window config N: finite multiset formed by the first N shell multisets after forgetting shell subtype certificates; count_window: multiplicity restricted by the strict condition dist(x,base)<N; sum_map_window: finite sum of an observable over the integer-ball window
m-14787af7903ed13a532f6228.proof_detail: Flatten the finite family of shell multisets indexed by range N. Use the uniqueness of shell membership and shellIndex<N iff dist<N to compute each point count. Apply multiset extensionality to the nested restriction identity. Distribute multiset maps and sums over the finite shell sum; combine the previously proved multiset-sum measurability.
m-14787af7903ed13a532f6228.adaptation: Integer open-ball restriction and finite shell sums implement bounded-window counting. Measurability follows from the code; continuity across a hard shell boundary is not asserted.

m-99a1933d6b89a1f6f1d7e93d.conditions: X is an arbitrary measurable standard-Borel space; no topology or physical order on X is assumed. The coding order is induced by a chosen measurable real embedding of X. FinitePointCloud is the enumerated carrier; Multiset X is order-forgetting.
m-99a1933d6b89a1f6f1d7e93d.relation_to_sources: The real embedding is justified by standard-Borel classification, not by the counting-measure formula. Chosen coding order, option padding and finite sorting-region decomposition are explicit local implementations; there is no topological order or continuity claim.
m-99a1933d6b89a1f6f1d7e93d.objects: codingLE: the pullback of real <= along a measurable embedding of X into the reals; OpLe: an order-like comparison on Option X putting padding none after present values; paddedCode multiset: length plus the sorted finite multiset sequence padded with none; IsSortedCode: the finite-presence condition and adjacent nondecreasing code comparisons; sortedCodeEquiv: bijection between finite multisets and the sorted-code subtype; Multiset measurable structure: the pullback sigma algebra of this injective sorted code
m-99a1933d6b89a1f6f1d7e93d.proof_detail: Use injectivity of the real embedding to obtain a total antisymmetric transitive coding relation; sort each multiset by it. Recover a multiset from a canonical nondecreasing option sequence and prove the code range characterization. Write the sorted-code range as countably many measurable finite-presence and neighboring-order constraints. Transfer standard-Borel structure from the measurable code range. For a fixed tuple length, partition into finitely many measurable sorting regions indexed by permutations; on each region the sorted code is a coordinate permutation. For varying length, split into countably many cardinality fibers and recover the finite tuple, proving the measurable order-forgetting projection.
m-99a1933d6b89a1f6f1d7e93d.adaptation: The real embedding is justified by standard-Borel classification, not by the counting-measure formula. Chosen coding order, option padding and finite sorting-region decomposition are explicit local implementations; there is no topological order or continuity claim.

m-705a3df60c5948a2fe8df3b7.conditions: Real normed domain/target without completeness or finite dimension; a continuous map on a convex domain, closed K, Lipschitz trace on K and actual derivative bound on its complement.
m-705a3df60c5948a2fe8df3b7.relation_to_sources: A normed-space closed-set refinement of the bounded-derivative mean-value estimate, proved directly and later applied to the actual derivative field.
m-705a3df60c5948a2fe8df3b7.objects: A Lipschitz estimate on the whole convex domain, and its global version with constant max(trace bound, complement bound).
m-705a3df60c5948a2fe8df3b7.proof_detail: Parametrize a segment and take its first and last encounters with K. Mean value and endpoint continuity control the two outside pieces; the trace Lipschitz bound controls the middle piece.
m-705a3df60c5948a2fe8df3b7.adaptation: A normed-space closed-set refinement of the bounded-derivative mean-value estimate, proved directly and later applied to the actual derivative field.

m-83bc5dc444b4557b3f096856.conditions: Real normed domain and target; finite weights, affine first jets, pointwise remainder/jet errors and local sum-one identity as required by each formula.
m-83bc5dc444b4557b3f096856.relation_to_sources: The first-order vector-valued form of Whitney’s Taylor-polynomial interpolation and cancellation; finite algebra helpers use only their displayed local hypotheses.
m-83bc5dc444b4557b3f096856.objects: Actual affine jets, their finite weighted blend, true first derivatives, partition-derivative cancellation and quantitative error bounds.
m-83bc5dc444b4557b3f096856.proof_detail: Differentiate finite scalar-weighted affine sums. Subtract one reference affine jet; the derivative of the local sum-one identity cancels the common terms, leaving controlled value and derivative discrepancies.
m-83bc5dc444b4557b3f096856.adaptation: The first-order vector-valued form of Whitney’s Taylor-polynomial interpolation and cancellation; finite algebra helpers use only their displayed local hypotheses.

m-4db24880c4af90259ec25a40.conditions: Real normed spaces; C2 finite weights with local sum one, prescribed affine jets and explicitly stated first-jet/value errors. No derivative of the prescribed jet field is assumed.
m-4db24880c4af90259ec25a40.relation_to_sources: A quantitative second-derivative consequence of the same Whitney interpolation. The numerical constants 15 and 6 are local estimates, not claimed as constants from the cited paper.
m-4db24880c4af90259ec25a40.objects: The actual second Fréchet derivative of a finite affine blend, reference-jet cancellation and a uniform boundary Hessian estimate from quadratic compatibility.
m-4db24880c4af90259ec25a40.proof_detail: Differentiate the finite affine blend twice; affine second derivatives vanish and the first/second weight sums cancel. Bound the remaining patch errors by Hessian weight mass and jet errors by twice the first derivative mass.
m-4db24880c4af90259ec25a40.adaptation: A quantitative second-derivative consequence of the same Whitney interpolation. The numerical constants 15 and 6 are local estimates, not claimed as constants from the cited paper.

m-5c66b0a835fa1aa6fd374ad6.conditions: A finite-dimensional real normed domain; positive radius for the support, plateau and radius-bound conclusions.
m-5c66b0a835fa1aa6fd374ad6.relation_to_sources: A ball-based normed-space replacement for the smooth localization used by Whitney. The particular bump formula and exact support balls are Lean constructions, not the original cube formula.
m-5c66b0a835fa1aa6fd374ad6.objects: One fixed compactly supported smooth bump and all translated/scaled ball bumps, with a common reciprocal-radius actual derivative bound.
m-5c66b0a835fa1aa6fd374ad6.proof_detail: Use a smooth unit bump with inner/outer radii 1 and 2, translate/rescale it, and transfer its bounded compactly supported derivative by the chain rule.
m-5c66b0a835fa1aa6fd374ad6.adaptation: A ball-based normed-space replacement for the smooth localization used by Whitney. The particular bump formula and exact support balls are Lean constructions, not the original cube formula.

m-63c8a047631c075a2b6e1632.conditions: Finite-dimensional real normed domain and nonempty closed K; the quantitative helper additionally exposes cover, local finiteness and enlarged-overlap assumptions.
m-63c8a047631c075a2b6e1632.relation_to_sources: The second-order instance of Whitney’s all-order partition estimate. The local norm estimates and actual finite-sum constants are proved directly.
m-63c8a047631c075a2b6e1632.objects: The very same normalized weights with locally finite Hessian support, first derivative mass O(r^-1) and true Hessian mass O(r^-2).
m-63c8a047631c075a2b6e1632.proof_detail: Reduce to a finite local weight family, show absent weights vanish as germs with all derivatives, and combine actual normalized-weight differentiation with the constructed bump bounds and overlap number.
m-63c8a047631c075a2b6e1632.adaptation: The second-order instance of Whitney’s all-order partition estimate. The local norm estimates and actual finite-sum constants are proved directly.

m-091fd5c463ab81f3f11f673f.conditions: Real normed domain for finite differential identities; finite dimension for the uniform bound on the actual scaled bump. C2 and positive normalization denominator are explicit where needed.

m-091fd5c463ab81f3f11f673f.objects: Actual product, sum and rescaled second derivatives; first/Hessian masses of normalized finite weights; inverse-square radius bound for bumps.
m-091fd5c463ab81f3f11f673f.proof_detail: Apply genuine Fréchet product/chain rules twice, use the local finite sum identity, and estimate operator norms. A fixed bump’s compact Hessian support supplies a uniform reference bound that rescales by r^-2.
m-091fd5c463ab81f3f11f673f.adaptation: Explicit differential estimates supporting the second-order partition scale in Whitney’s construction. The finite normalized-mass formulas are locally derived calculus, not a separate assumed extension theorem.

m-bf0d12bbbae709526f35d775.conditions: Finite-dimensional real normed domain/target and Borel measure structure; finite measured set and almost-everywhere full differentiability. Lipschitz variants use Haar measure or an absolutely continuous measure, and openness for local Lipschitz data.
m-bf0d12bbbae709526f35d775.relation_to_sources: An application of derivative measurability, Rademacher and Lusin; it does not yet assert uniform Whitney remainder or an extension.
m-bf0d12bbbae709526f35d775.objects: A compact set with arbitrarily small discarded mass, consisting of actual differentiability points where the original map and actual derivative are continuous.

m-bf0d12bbbae709526f35d775.adaptation: An application of derivative measurability, Rademacher and Lusin; it does not yet assert uniform Whitney remainder or an extension.

m-df90e104448009cdddd76337.conditions: Finite-dimensional Borel real normed domain, finite measured set and actual differentiability. The compact-subcore helper needs only a normed target; the full a.e./Lipschitz variants have finite-dimensional target.
m-df90e104448009cdddd76337.relation_to_sources: A full first-order compatibility preparation for the constructed C1 extension. It follows the uniformization idea in Whitney’s 1951 proof using a countable Lusin-index argument; no density-one-only remainder is substituted for the displayed pairwise compact-set condition.
m-df90e104448009cdddd76337.objects: Large compact restrictions carrying the original continuous first jet and a uniform first-order Whitney remainder condition.
m-df90e104448009cdddd76337.proof_detail: For every tolerance, measurably choose a discrete differentiability radius. Apply Lusin to the countable product of radius indices; compactness bounds each coordinate, giving a uniform radius. Combine with the differential Lusin core.
m-df90e104448009cdddd76337.adaptation: A full first-order compatibility preparation for the constructed C1 extension. It follows the uniformization idea in Whitney’s 1951 proof using a countable Lusin-index argument; no density-one-only remainder is substituted for the displayed pairwise compact-set condition.

    (∑ i : Fin (n + 1), fderiv ℝ (fun z ↦ φ z • j z) x (Pi.single i 1) i) =

/-- A smooth cutoff which is identically one on an open neighborhood of a compact
set inside the interior of a larger compact set. -/
theorem exists_contDiff_cutoff (K : Compacts (ι → ℝ)) {K₀ : Set (ι → ℝ)}
    (hK₀ : IsCompact K₀) (hK₀K : K₀ ⊆ interior (K : Set (ι → ℝ))) :
    ∃ χ : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ χ ∧
      Function.support χ ⊆ (K : Set (ι → ℝ)) ∧
      ∃ U : Set (ι → ℝ), IsOpen U ∧ K₀ ⊆ U ∧ ∀ x ∈ U, χ x = 1 := by
  have hmem : ∀ x : K₀, ∃ d : ℝ, 0 < d ∧
      closedBall x.1 d ⊆ interior (K : Set (ι → ℝ)) := by
    intro x
    exact Metric.nhds_basis_closedBall.mem_iff.1 (isOpen_interior.mem_nhds (hK₀K x.2))
  choose d hdpos hdsub using hmem
  let U : K₀ → Set (ι → ℝ) := fun x => ball x.1 (d x / 2)
  have hUopen : ∀ x, IsOpen (U x) := fun x => isOpen_ball
  have hcover : K₀ ⊆ ⋃ x : K₀, U x := by
    intro y hy
    exact mem_iUnion_of_mem ⟨y, hy⟩ (mem_ball_self (half_pos (hdpos ⟨y, hy⟩)))
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hK₀.elim_finite_subcover U hUopen hcover
  let bump : (x : K₀) → ContDiffBump x.1 := fun x =>
    ⟨d x / 2, 3 * d x / 4, half_pos (hdpos x), by linarith [hdpos x]⟩
  let χ : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ := fun y => 1 - ∏ x ∈ t, (1 - bump x y)
  have hprod_smooth : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun y => ∏ x ∈ t, (1 - bump x y)) := by
    classical
    refine Finset.induction_on t ?_ ?_
    · simpa only [Finset.prod_empty] using
        (contDiff_const : ContDiff ℝ ∞ fun _ : ι → ℝ => (1 : ℝ))
    · intro a s ha ih
      have h1 : (fun y : ι → ℝ => ∏ x ∈ insert a s, (1 - bump x y)) =
          (fun y => (1 - bump a y) * ∏ x ∈ s, (1 - bump x y)) := by
        funext y
        rw [Finset.prod_insert ha]
      rw [h1]
      exact (ContDiff.sub contDiff_const (bump a).contDiff).mul ih
  have hχsmooth : ContDiff ℝ ∞ χ := ContDiff.sub contDiff_const hprod_smooth
  have hbumpsupp : ∀ x : K₀, Function.support (bump x) ⊆ (K : Set (ι → ℝ)) := by
    intro x z hz
    have hz' : z ∈ ball x.1 (3 * (d x) / 4) := by
      rw [← (bump x).support_eq]
      exact hz
    have hzc : z ∈ closedBall x.1 (d x) :=
      Metric.closedBall_subset_closedBall (by linarith [hdpos x])
        (ball_subset_closedBall hz')
    exact interior_subset (hdsub x hzc)
  have hχsupp : Function.support χ ⊆ (K : Set (ι → ℝ)) := by
    intro y hy
    have hy' : y ∈ ⋃ x ∈ t, Function.support (bump x) := by
      by_contra h
      have hprod : ∏ x ∈ t, (1 - bump x y) = 1 := by
        refine Finset.prod_eq_one fun x hx => ?_
        have hb : bump x y = 0 := by
          by_contra hb
          exact h (mem_iUnion_of_mem x (mem_iUnion_of_mem hx
            (by simpa only [Function.mem_support] using hb)))
        rw [hb]
        ring
      exact (Function.mem_support.1 hy) (by simp only [χ, hprod, sub_self])
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hyx⟩ := by simpa only [mem_iUnion, exists_prop] using hy'
    exact hbumpsupp x hyx
  refine ⟨χ, hχsmooth, hχsupp, ⋃ x ∈ t, U x, ?_, ht, ?_⟩
  · exact isOpen_iUnion fun x => isOpen_iUnion fun _ => hUopen x
  · intro y hy
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hyx⟩ := by simpa only [mem_iUnion, exists_prop] using hy
    have hb : bump x y = 1 :=
      (bump x).one_of_mem_closedBall (ball_subset_closedBall hyx)
    have hprod : ∏ z ∈ t, (1 - bump z y) = 0 := by
      refine Finset.prod_eq_zero hx ?_
      rw [hb]
      ring
    simp only [χ, hprod, sub_zero]

    ∃ (N : ℕ) (S : Fin N → Set E),

      (Kᶜ ⊆ ⋃ i, ⋃ c ∈ S i, ball c (whitneyCoverRadius K c)) ∧
      (∀ i, ∀ c ∈ S i, closedBall c (2 * whitneyCoverRadius K c) ⊆ Kᶜ) ∧
      (∀ i, LocallyFinite (fun c : S i ↦
        {x : ↥(Kᶜ) | (x : E) ∈ closedBall (c : E) (2 * whitneyCoverRadius K c)})) ∧
      ∀ (x : E), x ∉ K → ∀ i,
        {c ∈ S i | x ∈ closedBall c ((5 / 2 : ℝ) * whitneyCoverRadius K c)}.Finite ∧

theorem exists_compact_cutoff_lipschitz_fderiv
    {G : E → F} {K : Set E} {L : ℝ≥0} {δ A : ℝ}
    (hK : IsCompact K) (hG : ContDiff ℝ 1 G) (hOff : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ G Kᶜ)
    (hLip : LipschitzOnWith L (fderiv ℝ G) K) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hnear : ∀ x ∉ K, infDist x K < δ → ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ G) x‖ ≤ A) :
    ∃ η : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ η ∧ HasCompactSupport η ∧
      (∀ x, η x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) ∧ (∀ x ∈ K, η =ᶠ[𝓝 x] fun _ ↦ 1) ∧
      let H : E → F := fun x ↦ η x • G x
      ContDiff ℝ 1 H ∧ HasCompactSupport H ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ H Kᶜ ∧
      EqOn H G K ∧ EqOn (fderiv ℝ H) (fderiv ℝ G) K ∧
      ∃ C : ℝ≥0, LipschitzWith C (fderiv ℝ H)

theorem hessian_whitneyBlend_cancel_apply (s : Finset ι) (φ : ι → E → ℝ)
    (f : E → F) (D : E → E →L[ℝ] F) (a : ι → E) {x b : E}
    (hφ : ∀ i ∈ s, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (φ i) x)
    (hone : (fun y ↦ ∑ i ∈ s, φ i y) =ᶠ[𝓝 x] fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) (v w : E) :
    fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (whitneyBlend s φ f D a)) x v w =
      ∑ i ∈ s, (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (φ i)) x v w •
          (whitneyAffineJet f D (a i) x - whitneyAffineJet f D b x) +
        fderiv ℝ (φ i) x v • (D (a i) - D b) w +
        fderiv ℝ (φ i) x w • (D (a i) - D b) v)

theorem exists_whitney_partition {K : Set E} (hK : IsClosed K) (hne : K.Nonempty) :
    ∃ (C : Set E) (ψ : C → E → ℝ) (A : ℝ), 0 ≤ A ∧ C ⊆ Kᶜ ∧
      (∀ c, tsupport (ψ c) ⊆ closedBall (c : E) (2 * whitneyCoverRadius K c)) ∧
      LocallyFinite (fun c : C ↦
        {x : ↥(Kᶜ) | (x : E) ∈ closedBall (c : E) (2 * whitneyCoverRadius K c)}) ∧
      ∀ (x : E), x ∉ K →
        (∀ c, 0 ≤ ψ c x) ∧ HasFiniteSupport (fun c ↦ ψ c x) ∧
        (∑ᶠ c, ψ c x) = 1 ∧ (∀ c, ContDiffAt ℝ ∞ (ψ c) x) ∧
        HasFiniteSupport (fun c ↦ fderiv ℝ (ψ c) x) ∧
        (∑ᶠ c, ‖fderiv ℝ (ψ c) x‖) ≤ A / whitneyCoverRadius K x

theorem exists_phaseWalkCode_cover_of_contractive_nodes {q m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m)
    {P : (Fin q → ℝ) → (Fin q → ℝ)} {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L)
    (hP : ∀ z w, ‖P z - P w‖ ≤ L * ‖z - w‖)
    (R : ℝ → (Fin q → ℝ) →L[ℝ] (Fin q → ℝ))
    (hsmall : ∀ r ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ‖R r‖ * L ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ))
    {ρ A : ℝ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) (hA : 0 ≤ A)
    (hR : ∀ r ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ‖R r‖ ≤ ρ)
    (hRLip : ∀ r ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      ‖R r - R s‖ ≤ A * |r - s|)
    (hroot : 2 * (ρ + 1) * ‖P 0‖ ≤ (m : ℝ))
    (hspeed : 4 * (1 + L) * A * ‖P 0‖ ≤ (m : ℝ)) :
    ∃ code : PhaseWalkCode (2 * q) m,
      ∀ r ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x p : Fin q → ℝ, ∀ a b : ℝ,
        ‖x + R r p‖ ≤ a → ‖p - P x‖ ≤ b →
        ∃ j : Fin (m + 1),
          ‖phasePairVector x p - phaseWalkVertex code j‖ ≤
            max (2 * (a + ρ * b)) (b + 2 * L * (a + ρ * b)) + 2

      ‖R r - R s‖ ≤ A * |r - s|) :

      (∀ r ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, z r + R r (P (z r)) = 0) ∧

d-900a1b33029ef9649d77843c.declaration_documentation: **Differentiability of a concave pressure from interval slopes.** If `p` is concave near zero and, along a sequence `t n > 0` tending to zero, the interval slopes over `[t n, 2 t n]` and `[-2 t n, -t n]` share a limit `d`, then `p` is differentiable at zero with derivative `d`. This is the final analytic step of the paper's differentiability proof: the interval slopes are supplied by the opposite-tilt optima, and the common diffuse representation makes their two limits coincide.

    (hintervalPos : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (p (2 * t n) - p (t n)) / t n) atTop (𝓝 d))
    (hintervalNeg : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (p (-(t n)) - p (-(2 * t n))) / t n)

d-380c7299ca36ad4fb0aa0749.name: OTSelector.hasDerivAt_of_concave_supergradient_sequence
d-380c7299ca36ad4fb0aa0749.declaration_documentation: **Finite-level supergradients give differentiability of the limit.** Let `p` be concave near zero and let `p n` approximate `p` uniformly with error `δ n`, where `δ n / t n → 0`. Suppose `q⁺ n` and `q⁻ n` are bracketed by the right and left secant data at `± t n`: `interval⁺ ≤ q⁺ ≤ rightSecant`, `leftSecant ≤ q⁻ ≤ interval⁻`, and both sequences converge to `d`. Then `p` is differentiable at zero with derivative `d`. This is the paper's differentiability argument reduced to its final form: the uniform error is `o(t n)`, the probes of the opposite tilted optima supply the brackets, and the common diffuse representation gives the common limit.
d-380c7299ca36ad4fb0aa0749.name_identity_policy: Current explicit rename is applied when recorded; private/native names otherwise denote the immutable inspected source identity, with current source_name preserved.
d-380c7299ca36ad4fb0aa0749.exact_source_header:
theorem hasDerivAt_of_concave_supergradient_sequence {p : ℝ → ℝ} {pn : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ}
    {δ : ℕ → ℝ} {t qpos qneg : ℕ → ℝ} {ε d : ℝ}
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hconc : ConcaveOn ℝ (Ioo (-ε) ε) p)
    (hconv : ∀ n, ∀ s ∈ Ioo (-ε) ε, |pn n s - p s| ≤ δ n)
    (hδ : Tendsto (fun n => δ n / t n) atTop (𝓝 0))
    (htpos : ∀ n, 0 < t n) (ht : Tendsto t atTop (𝓝 (0 : ℝ)))
    (htsmall : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, 2 * t n < ε)
    (hposLow : ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      (pn n (2 * t n) - pn n (t n)) / t n ≤ qpos n)
    (hposHigh : ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      qpos n ≤ (pn n (t n) - pn n 0) / t n)
    (hnegLow : ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      (pn n 0 - pn n (-(t n))) / t n ≤ qneg n)
    (hnegHigh : ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      qneg n ≤ (pn n (-(t n)) - pn n (-(2 * t n))) / t n)
    (hqpos : Tendsto qpos atTop (𝓝 d)) (hqneg : Tendsto qneg atTop (𝓝 d)) :
    HasDerivAt p d 0

d-7060402cd691e73f65634ff7.declaration_documentation: **Common supergradient differences force differentiability.** The same finite-level squeeze as `hasDerivAt_of_concave_supergradient_sequence`, but the stochastic input is only that the two opposite-tilt probe costs share a limit: `qpos n - qneg n → 0`. The common one-sided limit is then produced by the concavity squeeze.

theorem hasDerivAt_of_concave_supergradient_sequence_of_diff {p : ℝ → ℝ} {pn : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ}
    {δ : ℕ → ℝ} {t qpos qneg : ℕ → ℝ} {ε : ℝ}
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hconc : ConcaveOn ℝ (Ioo (-ε) ε) p)
    (hconv : ∀ n, ∀ s ∈ Ioo (-ε) ε, |pn n s - p s| ≤ δ n)
    (hδ : Tendsto (fun n => δ n / t n) atTop (𝓝 0))
    (htpos : ∀ n, 0 < t n) (ht : Tendsto t atTop (𝓝 (0 : ℝ)))
    (htsmall : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, 2 * t n < ε)
    (hposLow : ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      (pn n (2 * t n) - pn n (t n)) / t n ≤ qpos n)
    (hposHigh : ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      qpos n ≤ (pn n (t n) - pn n 0) / t n)
    (hnegLow : ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      (pn n 0 - pn n (-(t n))) / t n ≤ qneg n)
    (hnegHigh : ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      qneg n ≤ (pn n (-(t n)) - pn n (-(2 * t n))) / t n)
    (hdiff : Tendsto (fun n => qpos n - qneg n) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    ∃ d : ℝ, HasDerivAt p d 0

d-766f76f0b5d3d96c06c930ca.name: OTSelector.hasDerivAt_of_intervalSlope_tendsto
d-766f76f0b5d3d96c06c930ca.declaration_documentation: **Common interval-slope limit gives differentiability.** Suppose the two one-sided secant slopes at zero have (real) limits `Lp`, `Lm`, and along a sequence `t n > 0` tending to zero the interval slopes over `[t n, 2 t n]` and over `[-2 t n, - t n]` have a common limit `d`. Then `Lp = Lm = d` and `p` is differentiable at zero with derivative `d`. This packages the final step of the paper's differentiability proof: the one-sided derivative limits are read off from the tilted optima, and the common diffuse representation supplies the common interval-slope limit.
d-766f76f0b5d3d96c06c930ca.name_identity_policy: Current explicit rename is applied when recorded; private/native names otherwise denote the immutable inspected source identity, with current source_name preserved.

theorem hasDerivAt_of_intervalSlope_tendsto {p : ℝ → ℝ} {t : ℕ → ℝ} {d Lp Lm : ℝ}
    (htpos : ∀ n, 0 < t n) (ht : Tendsto t atTop (𝓝 (0 : ℝ)))
    (hslopePos : Tendsto (fun h : ℝ => (p h - p 0) / h) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 Lp))
    (hslopeNeg : Tendsto (fun h : ℝ => (p 0 - p (-h)) / h) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 Lm))
    (hintervalPos : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (p (2 * t n) - p (t n)) / t n) atTop (𝓝 d))
    (hintervalNeg : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (p (-(t n)) - p (-(2 * t n))) / t n)
      atTop (𝓝 d)) :
    HasDerivAt p d 0

theorem hasDerivAt_of_concave_mean_of_curry_supergradient_gap
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (pn : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ) (pressure : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hconc : ∀ n, ConcaveOn ℝ (Ioo (-ε) ε) (pn n))
    (hpt : ∀ s ∈ Ioo (-ε) ε,
      Tendsto (fun n ↦ pn n s) atTop (𝓝 (pressure s)))

theorem concave_le_extrapolation {f : ℝ → ℝ} {s : Set ℝ} (hf : ConcaveOn ℝ s f)
    {u a x : ℝ} (hu : u ∈ s) (ha : a ∈ s) (hx : x ∈ s) (hua : u < a) (hax : a ≤ x) :
    f x ≤ ((x - u) * f a - (x - a) * f u) / (a - u)

d-6d2b0e0fb179000729e164dd.declaration_documentation: **Lower affine bound for a concave function.** If `f` is concave on `s` and `a ≤ x ≤ b`, then `f x` is at least the chord through `(a, f a)` and `(b, f b)` evaluated at `x`.

theorem concave_ge_interpolation {f : ℝ → ℝ} {s : Set ℝ} (hf : ConcaveOn ℝ s f)

d-d269919de93283c2d5fd5932.declaration_documentation: **Three-point bound for a concave function.** On `[a, b]`, a concave `f` is bounded by a constant (depending only on the positions) times the sum of `|f|` at `u`, `a`, `b`, where `u < a`.

theorem abs_le_of_concaveOn_three_points {f : ℝ → ℝ} {s : Set ℝ} (hf : ConcaveOn ℝ s f)
    {u a b x : ℝ} (hu : u ∈ s) (ha : a ∈ s) (hb : b ∈ s) (hx : x ∈ s)
    (hua : u < a) (hab : a < b) (hb0 : 0 ≤ b) (hax : a ≤ x) (hxb : x ≤ b) :
    |f x| ≤ (((b + |u|) + (b + |a|)) / (a - u) + 1) * (|f u| + |f a| + |f b|)

theorem quadraticSoftMinimum_dual_endpoints
    {ε δ M : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    (u : I → ℝ) (v : J → ℝ) (x : I → H) (y : J → H)
    (hdual : ∀ i j, u i + v j ≤ ‖y j - x i‖ ^ 2 / 2)
    (hcost : ∀ i j, ‖y j - x i‖ ^ 2 / 2 ≤ M) (i : I) (j : J) :

      M * δ + ε * Real.log (Fintype.card I)

theorem quadraticSoftMinimum_hamiltonJacobi
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [Nonempty I]
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε ≠ 0) (a : I → ℝ) (y : I → H)
    (τ : ℝ) (hτ : τ ≠ 0) (x : H) :
    let F := fun i σ z ↦ quadraticHamiltonJacobiBranch (a i) (y i) σ z
    let w := finiteSoftMinimumWeight ε (fun i ↦ F i τ x)
    let p := ∑ i, w i • (τ⁻¹ • (x - y i))
    let d := ∑ i, w i * (-‖x - y i‖ ^ 2 / (2 * τ ^ 2))
    HasDerivAt (fun σ ↦ finiteSoftMinimum ε (fun i ↦ F i σ x)) d τ ∧
    HasGradientAt (fun z ↦ finiteSoftMinimum ε (fun i ↦ F i τ z)) p x ∧
    d + ‖p‖ ^ 2 / 2 ≤ 0

theorem finiteSoftMinimum_hamiltonJacobi
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε ≠ 0) (F : I → ℝ → H → ℝ) (d : I → ℝ) (p : I → H)
    (τ : ℝ) (x : H)
    (ht : ∀ i, HasDerivAt (fun σ ↦ F i σ x) (d i) τ)
    (hx : ∀ i, HasGradientAt (F i τ) (p i) x)
    (hHJ : ∀ i, d i + ‖p i‖ ^ 2 / 2 ≤ 0) :

    HasDerivAt (fun σ ↦ finiteSoftMinimum ε (fun i ↦ F i σ x)) (∑ i, w i * d i) τ ∧
    HasGradientAt (fun y ↦ finiteSoftMinimum ε (fun i ↦ F i τ y)) (∑ i, w i • p i) x ∧

    {f : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ} {G : ℝ} (hG : 0 ≤ G)
    (hbdd : ∀ t, ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ R : ℝ, 1 ≤ R → |f R t| ≤ B)
    (hconcave : ∀ R, ConcaveOn ℝ univ (f R))
    (hlip : ∀ R t u, |f R t - f R u| ≤ G * |t - u|)
    (hcont : ∀ t L, 0 < L → Tendsto (fun R ↦ f R t) (𝓝 L) (𝓝 (f L t)))
    (ε : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hεcont : ∀ L, 0 < L → Tendsto ε (𝓝 L) (𝓝 (ε L)))
    (hε0 : Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0))
    (hblock : ∀ t L : ℝ, 0 < L → ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
      ∀ᶠ m : ℕ in atTop, f ((m : ℝ) * L) t ≤ f L t + ε L + δ) :

/-- Orthogonality to every genuine translation difference is exactly
invariance under every translation. -/
theorem orthogonal_translationCoboundarySpan
    (U : F → H ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] H) :
    (translationCoboundarySpan U)ᗮ = translationFixedSubspace U ⊤ := by
  ext x
  constructor
  · intro hx a _
    have h := hx (U a x - x) (Submodule.subset_span ⟨(a, x), rfl⟩)
    rw [inner_sub_left, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq] at h
    apply eq_of_norm_le_re_inner_eq_norm_sq (𝕜 := ℝ) ((U a).norm_map x).le
    simpa only [RCLike.re_to_real] using sub_eq_zero.1 h
  · intro hx
    have hsub : translationCoboundarySpan U ≤ (ℝ ∙ x)ᗮ := by
      apply Submodule.span_le.2
      rintro y ⟨⟨a, z⟩, rfl⟩
      change U a z - z ∈ (ℝ ∙ x)ᗮ
      apply Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_left.2
      rw [inner_sub_left]
      have hfixed := hx a (by trivial)
      have he : ⟪U a z, x⟫_ℝ = ⟪z, x⟫_ℝ := by
        calc
          _ = ⟪U a z, U a x⟫_ℝ := by rw [hfixed]
          _ = _ := (U a).inner_map_map z x
      exact sub_eq_zero.2 he
    intro y hy
    exact Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_left.1 (hsub hy)

d-9d1526fbff0ca46ccdfe759a.selected_source_excerpt:
/-- Uniform contractions that annihilate every actual translation
difference annihilate the full orthogonal complement of joint invariants.
This is the dense Hilbert extension step used after the concrete box-shell
estimate has established the coboundary limits. -/
theorem tendsto_contractions_zero_of_translation_coboundaries
    {J : Type*} (l : Filter J) (U : F → H ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] H)
    (A : J → H →L[ℝ] H) (hA : ∀ j, ‖A j‖ ≤ 1)
    (hcob : ∀ a y, Tendsto (fun j ↦ A j (U a y - y)) l (𝓝 0))
    {x : H} (hx : x ∈ (translationFixedSubspace U ⊤)ᗮ) :
    Tendsto (fun j ↦ A j x) l (𝓝 0) := by
  let Z : Submodule ℝ H :=
    { carrier := {x | Tendsto (fun j ↦ A j x) l (𝓝 0)}
      zero_mem' := by
        change Tendsto (fun j ↦ A j 0) l (𝓝 0)
        simpa only [map_zero] using
          (tendsto_const_nhds : Tendsto (fun _ : J ↦ (0 : H)) l (𝓝 0))
      add_mem' := by
        intro x y hx hy
        change Tendsto (fun j ↦ A j (x + y)) l (𝓝 0)
        simpa only [map_add, zero_add] using hx.add hy
      smul_mem' := by
        intro c x hx
        change Tendsto (fun j ↦ A j (c • x)) l (𝓝 0)
        simpa only [map_smul, smul_zero] using hx.const_smul c }
  have hequi : Equicontinuous (fun j x ↦ A j x) := by
    apply Metric.equicontinuous_of_continuity_modulus id tendsto_id
    intro x y j
    change dist (A j x) (A j y) ≤ dist x y
    rw [dist_eq_norm, ← map_sub, dist_eq_norm]
    simpa only [one_mul] using (A j).le_of_opNorm_le (hA j) (x - y)
  have hclosed : IsClosed (Z : Set H) :=
    hequi.isClosed_setOfPred_tendsto continuous_const
  have hspan : translationCoboundarySpan U ≤ Z := by
    apply Submodule.span_le.2
    rintro y ⟨⟨a, z⟩, rfl⟩
    exact hcob a z
  have hclosure := (translationCoboundarySpan U).topologicalClosure_minimal hspan hclosed
  rw [closure_translationCoboundarySpan] at hclosure
  exact hclosure hx

of the original translations in the ACTUAL range of the coordinate map. -/

theorem chartGraph_parameter_matrices (hF : F.IsSmoothStronglyConvex) (x₀ : M)
    (bW : Basis ι ℝ W) (bV : Basis ι ℝ V)
    {g : OpenPartialHomeomorph ((ℝ × V) × V) ((ℝ × V) × (V →L[ℝ] ℝ))}
    (hg : (g : ((ℝ × V) × V) → ((ℝ × V) × (V →L[ℝ] ℝ))) =
      parametricLegendre (F.chartGraphLagrangian x₀))
    (hsub : g.source ⊆ (extChartAt 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ × V) x₀).target ×ˢ univ)
    (hG : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ g.symm g.target)
    {Ψ : W × ℝ → V × (V →L[ℝ] ℝ)} {D : Set (W × ℝ)}
    (hD : IsOpen D) (hΨ : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 Ψ D)
    (hODE : ∀ z ∈ D, HasDerivAt (fun s ↦ Ψ (z.1, s))
      (GraphHamiltonian.field (F.chartGraphLagrangian x₀) g z.2 (Ψ z)) z.2)
    {w₀ : W} {t : ℝ} (hz : (w₀, t) ∈ D)
    (hp : ((t, (Ψ (w₀, t)).1), (Ψ (w₀, t)).2) ∈ g.target)
    (hinj : Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (fun w ↦ Ψ (w, t)) w₀))
    (hpair : ∀ u v : W, canonicalPhasePairing
      (fderiv ℝ (fun w ↦ Ψ (w, t)) w₀ u)
      (fderiv ℝ (fun w ↦ Ψ (w, t)) w₀ v) = 0) :
    let L := F.chartGraphLagrangian x₀
    let Z := fun s ↦ fderiv ℝ (fun w ↦ Ψ (w, s)) w₀
    let J := fun s ↦ vectorFamilyMatrix bV (fun j ↦ (Z s (bW j)).1)
    let P := fun s ↦ covectorFamilyMatrix bV (fun j ↦ (Z s (bW j)).2)
    let A := hamiltonianMatrixA bV (GraphHamiltonian.blockA L g t (Ψ (w₀, t)))
    let B := hamiltonianMatrixB bV (GraphHamiltonian.blockB L g t (Ψ (w₀, t)))
    let C := hamiltonianMatrixC bV (GraphHamiltonian.blockC L g t (Ψ (w₀, t)))
    HasDerivAt J (B * J t + C * P t) t ∧
      HasDerivAt P (-A * J t - Bᵀ * P t) t ∧ Aᵀ = A ∧ Cᵀ = C ∧ C.PosDef ∧
      (J t)ᵀ * P t = (P t)ᵀ * J t ∧
      (∀ u : ι → ℝ, J t *ᵥ u = 0 → P t *ᵥ u = 0 → u = 0) ∧
      C = hamiltonianMatrixC bV (ContinuousLinearMap.inverse
        (GraphLegendre.verticalHessian L (g.symm ((t, (Ψ (w₀, t)).1),
          (Ψ (w₀, t)).2))))

theorem norm_le_endpoint_norm_mul_exp
    {f f' : ℝ → E} {a b c L : ℝ}
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b))
    (hf : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt f (f' t) t)
    (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hg : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, ‖f' t‖ ≤ L * ‖f t‖)
    (hc : c ∈ Ioo a b) {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Icc a b) :
    ‖f c‖ ≤ ‖f t‖ * Real.exp (L * (b - a)) := by
  have hcl : t ∈ closure (Ioo a b) := by
    rw [closure_Ioo (hc.1.trans hc.2).ne]
    exact ht
  have : NeBot (𝓝[Ioo a b] t) := mem_closure_iff_nhdsWithin_neBot.mp hcl
  apply ge_of_tendsto
    (((hcont t ht).mono Ioo_subset_Icc_self).norm.mul_const (Real.exp (L * (b - a))))
  filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with s hs
  exact norm_le_exp_of_norm_deriv_le_mul hf hL hg hs hc

/-- A zero value anywhere on the closed interval forces every interior value to vanish. -/
theorem eq_zero_of_endpoint_eq_zero_of_norm_deriv_le_mul
    {f f' : ℝ → E} {a b c L : ℝ}
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b))
    (hf : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt f (f' t) t)
    (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hg : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, ‖f' t‖ ≤ L * ‖f t‖)
    (hc : c ∈ Ioo a b) {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Icc a b) (hzero : f t = 0) :
    f c = 0 := by
  apply norm_eq_zero.mp
  apply le_antisymm _ (norm_nonneg _)
  simpa only [hzero, norm_zero, zero_mul] using
    norm_le_endpoint_norm_mul_exp hcont hf hL hg hc ht

/-- Zero at any closed-interval point forces a continuous Hamiltonian pair to vanish
at every interior point; only interior ODE equations are needed. -/
theorem hamiltonian_pair_eq_zero_of_endpoint_eq_zero
    {J P A B C : ℝ → Matrix n n ℝ} {a b c : ℝ}
    (hJcont : ContinuousOn J (Icc a b)) (hPcont : ContinuousOn P (Icc a b))
    (hJ : ∀ s ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt J (B s * J s + C s * P s) s)
    (hP : ∀ s ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt P (-A s * J s - (B s)ᵀ * P s) s)
    (hA : ContinuousOn A (Icc a b)) (hB : ContinuousOn B (Icc a b))
    (hC : ContinuousOn C (Icc a b)) (hc : c ∈ Ioo a b)
    {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Icc a b) (hJt : J t = 0) (hPt : P t = 0) :
    J c = 0 ∧ P c = 0 := by
  have hBT : ContinuousOn (fun s ↦ (B s)ᵀ) (Icc a b) :=
    continuous_id.matrix_transpose.comp_continuousOn hB
  have hg : ContinuousOn (fun s ↦ ‖A s‖ + ‖B s‖ + ‖C s‖ + ‖(B s)ᵀ‖) (Icc a b) :=
    ((hA.norm.add hB.norm).add hC.norm).add hBT.norm
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := isCompact_Icc.bddAbove_image hg
  let f : ℝ → Matrix n n ℝ × Matrix n n ℝ := fun s ↦ (J s, P s)
  let f' : ℝ → Matrix n n ℝ × Matrix n n ℝ :=
    fun s ↦ (B s * J s + C s * P s, -A s * J s - (B s)ᵀ * P s)
  have hf : ∀ s ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt f (f' s) s := fun s hs ↦
    (hJ s hs).prodMk (hP s hs)
  have hbound : ∀ s ∈ Ioo a b, ‖f' s‖ ≤ max L 0 * ‖f s‖ := by
    intro s hs
    exact (norm_hamiltonian_pair_le (A s) (B s) (C s) (J s) (P s)).trans
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
        ((hL (mem_image_of_mem _ (Ioo_subset_Icc_self hs))).trans (le_max_left _ _))
        (norm_nonneg _))
  have hzero : f t = 0 := by simp [f, hJt, hPt]
  have hz := eq_zero_of_endpoint_eq_zero_of_norm_deriv_le_mul
    (hJcont.prodMk hPcont) hf (le_max_right L 0) hbound hc ht hzero
  exact ⟨congrArg Prod.fst hz, congrArg Prod.snd hz⟩

/-- A differential linear-growth bound gives a uniform bound on a finite open interval. -/
theorem norm_le_exp_of_norm_deriv_le_mul
    {f f' : ℝ → E} {a b c L : ℝ}
    (hf : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt f (f' t) t)
    (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hg : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, ‖f' t‖ ≤ L * ‖f t‖)
    (hc : c ∈ Ioo a b) {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Ioo a b) :
    ‖f t‖ ≤ ‖f c‖ * Real.exp (L * (b - a)) := by
  let g : ℝ → ℝ := AffineMap.lineMap c t
  have hmaps : MapsTo g (Icc 0 1) (Ioo a b) := (convex_Ioo a b).mapsTo_lineMap hc ht
  have hd : ∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      HasDerivAt (f ∘ g) ((t - c) • f' (g s)) s := by
    intro s hs
    exact (hf (g s) (hmaps hs)).scomp s AffineMap.hasDerivAt_lineMap
  have hcont : ContinuousOn (f ∘ g) (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :=
    fun s hs ↦ (hd s hs).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
  have hbound : ∀ s ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1,
      ‖(t - c) • f' (g s)‖ ≤ (L * |t - c|) * ‖(f ∘ g) s‖ + 0 := by
    intro s hs
    rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, add_zero]
    calc
      |t - c| * ‖f' (g s)‖ ≤ |t - c| * (L * ‖f (g s)‖) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hg _ (hmaps (Ico_subset_Icc_self hs))) (abs_nonneg _)
      _ = (L * |t - c|) * ‖(f ∘ g) s‖ := by dsimp; ring
  have hbnd := norm_le_gronwallBound_of_norm_deriv_right_le hcont
    (fun s hs ↦ (hd s (Ico_subset_Icc_self hs)).hasDerivWithinAt)
    (le_refl ‖(f ∘ g) 0‖) hbound 1 (by simp)
  have hdist : |t - c| ≤ b - a := by
    rw [abs_le]
    constructor <;> linarith [hc.1, hc.2, ht.1, ht.2]
  have hpre : ‖f t‖ ≤ ‖f c‖ * Real.exp (L * |t - c|) := by
    simpa [g, gronwallBound_ε0] using hbnd
  exact hpre.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
    (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hdist hL)) (norm_nonneg _))

/-- A direct operator-norm growth bound for the Hamiltonian matrix field. -/
theorem norm_hamiltonian_pair_le (A B C K R : Matrix n n ℝ) :
    ‖(B * K + C * R, -A * K - Bᵀ * R)‖ ≤
      (‖A‖ + ‖B‖ + ‖C‖ + ‖Bᵀ‖) * ‖(K, R)‖ := by
  have hK : ‖K‖ ≤ ‖(K, R)‖ := norm_fst_le (K, R)
  have hR : ‖R‖ ≤ ‖(K, R)‖ := norm_snd_le (K, R)
  rw [Prod.norm_def]
  apply max_le
  · calc
      ‖B * K + C * R‖ ≤ ‖B * K‖ + ‖C * R‖ := norm_add_le _ _
      _ ≤ ‖B‖ * ‖K‖ + ‖C‖ * ‖R‖ := add_le_add (norm_mul_le _ _) (norm_mul_le _ _)
      _ ≤ (‖B‖ + ‖C‖) * ‖(K, R)‖ := by
        rw [add_mul]
        exact add_le_add (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hK (norm_nonneg _))
          (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hR (norm_nonneg _))
      _ ≤ _ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
        (by linarith [norm_nonneg A, norm_nonneg B, norm_nonneg C, norm_nonneg Bᵀ])
        (norm_nonneg _)
  · calc
      ‖-A * K - Bᵀ * R‖ ≤ ‖-A * K‖ + ‖Bᵀ * R‖ := norm_sub_le _ _
      _ ≤ ‖-A‖ * ‖K‖ + ‖Bᵀ‖ * ‖R‖ := add_le_add (norm_mul_le _ _) (norm_mul_le _ _)
      _ = ‖A‖ * ‖K‖ + ‖Bᵀ‖ * ‖R‖ := by rw [norm_neg]
      _ ≤ (‖A‖ + ‖Bᵀ‖) * ‖(K, R)‖ := by
        rw [add_mul]
        exact add_le_add (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hK (norm_nonneg _))
          (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hR (norm_nonneg _))
      _ ≤ _ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
        (by linarith [norm_nonneg A, norm_nonneg B, norm_nonneg C, norm_nonneg Bᵀ])
        (norm_nonneg _)

theorem optimalAssignment_iff_cavity (cost : Fin (n + 1) → Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)

      (∑ i, α i) + ∑ j, β j = perturbedAssignmentValue cost 0 0 ∧

        ∀ i, α i + β (σ i) = cost i (σ i)

theorem exists_capacity_assignment_dual {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (r : α → ℕ) (htotal : ∑ j, r j = n + 1) (hr : ∀ j, 0 < r j)
    (cost : Fin (n + 1) → α → ℝ) :
    ∃ (u : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (v : α → ℝ),
      (∀ i j, u i + v j ≤ cost i j) ∧
      (∀ a, OptimalCapacityAssignment r cost a ↔
        CapacityFeasible r a ∧ ∀ i, u i + v (a i) = cost i (a i)) ∧
      ∃ a, OptimalCapacityAssignment r cost a ∧
        capacityAssignmentCost cost a = (∑ i, u i) + ∑ j, (r j : ℝ) * v j

theorem card_eq_sum_min_of_cell_max
    {X C : Type*} [Fintype C] [DecidableEq C] {a b : ℕ}
    (leaf : X → C) (x : Fin a → X) (y : Fin b → X) (σ : PartialMatching a b)

          ((Finset.univ.filter (fun j => leaf (y j) = c)).card)) :

                            ((Finset.univ.filter (fun j => leaf (y j) = c)).card)

d-3cdf21693215c2ca1fe74c20.name: OTSelector.exists_maxCardMatching_le_add_repair
d-3cdf21693215c2ca1fe74c20.declaration_documentation: **Two-level block repair.** If `σ0` is supported inside the cells of the finite partition `leaf` and is maximum-cardinality in every `leaf` cell, then it can be extended to a matching that is maximum-cardinality in every cell of the coarser partition `coarse`. The number of repair edges is one half of the decrease of the total absolute cell-count discrepancy from `leaf` to `coarse`, and each repair edge costs at most `B`.

theorem exists_maxCardMatching_le_add_repair
    {X C D : Type*} [Fintype C] [DecidableEq C] [Fintype D] [DecidableEq D]
    (leaf : X → C) (coarse : X → D)
    (hcompat : ∀ u v : X, leaf u = leaf v → coarse u = coarse v)
    {a b : ℕ} (x : Fin a → X) (y : Fin b → X)
    (cost : Fin a → Fin b → ℝ) (σ0 : PartialMatching a b)
    (hleaf : ∀ e ∈ σ0.edges, leaf (x e.1) = leaf (y e.2))
    (hmax : ∀ c : C, (σ0.edges.filter (fun e => leaf (x e.1) = c)).card =
      min ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i => leaf (x i) = c)).card)
          ((Finset.univ.filter (fun j => leaf (y j) = c)).card))
    (B : ℝ) (hB : ∀ i j, coarse (x i) = coarse (y j) → cost i j ≤ B) :
    ∃ σ : PartialMatching a b,
      (∀ e ∈ σ.edges, coarse (x e.1) = coarse (y e.2)) ∧
      (∀ d : D, (σ.edges.filter (fun e => coarse (x e.1) = d)).card =
        min ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i => coarse (x i) = d)).card)
            ((Finset.univ.filter (fun j => coarse (y j) = d)).card)) ∧
      σ.card = ∑ d : D, min ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i => coarse (x i) = d)).card)
                             ((Finset.univ.filter (fun j => coarse (y j) = d)).card) ∧
      σ.cost cost ≤ σ0.cost cost + B * ((1 / 2 : ℝ) *
        ((∑ c : C, |partitionCount (leaf ∘ x) c - partitionCount (leaf ∘ y) c|) -
         (∑ d : D, |partitionCount (coarse ∘ x) d - partitionCount (coarse ∘ y) d|)))

theorem card_eq_min_of_root
    {X C : Type*} [Fintype C] [DecidableEq C] {a b : ℕ}
    (leaf : X → C) (x : Fin a → X) (y : Fin b → X)
    (hroot : ∀ u v : X, leaf u = leaf v)
    (σ : PartialMatching a b)
    (hmax : ∀ c : C, (σ.edges.filter (fun e => leaf (x e.1) = c)).card =
      min ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i => leaf (x i) = c)).card)
          ((Finset.univ.filter (fun j => leaf (y j) = c)).card)) :
    σ.card = min a b

d-0bbd1670abe4b07b02bd2d18.name: OTSelector.exists_maxCardMatching_le_add_hierarchical_repair
d-0bbd1670abe4b07b02bd2d18.declaration_documentation: **Hierarchical block repair.** Let `cell k` be a nested family of finite partitions, with `cell 0` the root (all points in one cell) and `cell K` the finest partition. Suppose `σ0` is supported inside the finest cells and is maximum-cardinality in every finest cell, and suppose every pair of points that lies in a common level-`k` cell has cost at most `B (k+1)`. Then `σ0` extends to a globally maximum-cardinality matching whose cost exceeds the cost of `σ0` by at most the sum over `k = 1, ..., K` of `B k` times one half of the increase of the total absolute cell-count discrepancy from level `k-1` to level `k`. No nonnegativity assumption on the edge costs is used.
d-0bbd1670abe4b07b02bd2d18.name_identity_policy: Current explicit rename is applied when recorded; private/native names otherwise denote the immutable inspected source identity, with current source_name preserved.
d-0bbd1670abe4b07b02bd2d18.exact_source_header:
theorem exists_maxCardMatching_le_add_hierarchical_repair
    {X : Type*} {K : ℕ} {C : ℕ → Type*}
    [∀ k, Fintype (C k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (C k)]
    (cell : (k : ℕ) → X → C k)
    (hnested : ∀ (k l : ℕ), k ≤ l → ∀ u v : X,
      cell l u = cell l v → cell k u = cell k v)
    {a b : ℕ} (x : Fin a → X) (y : Fin b → X)
    (cost : Fin a → Fin b → ℝ)
    (σ0 : PartialMatching a b)
    (hleaf : ∀ e ∈ σ0.edges, cell K (x e.1) = cell K (y e.2))
    (hmax : ∀ c : C K,
      (σ0.edges.filter (fun e => cell K (x e.1) = c)).card =
        min ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i => cell K (x i) = c)).card)
            ((Finset.univ.filter (fun j => cell K (y j) = c)).card))
    (B : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hB : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < K → ∀ i j,
      cell k (x i) = cell k (y j) → cost i j ≤ B (k + 1))
    (hroot : ∀ u v : X, cell 0 u = cell 0 v) :
    ∃ σ : PartialMatching a b,
      σ.card = min a b ∧
      σ.cost cost ≤ σ0.cost cost +
        ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (K + 1), if 0 < k then
          B k * (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
            ((∑ c : C k,
                |partitionCount (cell k ∘ x) c - partitionCount (cell k ∘ y) c|) -
             (∑ p : C (k - 1),
                |partitionCount (cell (k - 1) ∘ x) p -
                 partitionCount (cell (k - 1) ∘ y) p|))
        else 0

theorem optimalCapacityAssignment_iff_capacityVacancyPotentials_tight
    (r : α → ℕ) (htotal : ∑ j, r j = n + 1) (hr : ∀ j, 0 < r j)
    (cost : Fin (n + 1) → α → ℝ) (i₀ : Fin (n + 1)) (j : α) (a : Fin n → α) :

theorem normalizedClockClassFlow_marginals
    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J]
    (d : ℝ) (hd : 0 < d) (P : I → J → ℝ) (a : I → ℝ) (b : J → ℝ)
    (allowed : I → J → Prop)
    (hP : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ P i j)
    (hrow : ∀ i, ∑ j, P i j = d * a i)
    (hcol : ∀ j, ∑ i, P i j = d * b j)
    (hzero : ∀ i j, ¬ allowed i j → P i j = 0) :
    (∀ i j, 0 ≤ P i j / d) ∧
    (∀ i, ∑ j, P i j / d = a i) ∧
    (∀ j, ∑ i, P i j / d = b j) ∧
    ∀ i j, ¬ allowed i j → P i j / d = 0

theorem normalized_referenceResidual_mass_le

d-fd4d00ba78986c03cb8ce634.declaration_documentation: A matching obtained from the model optimum by retaining a common core and repairing it gives a relative comparison with the exact repair kinetic cost. The repair may depend on the entire coupled sample.

theorem maxCardValue_le_relative_common_core_add_repair
    {c c' g g' : Fin m → Fin n → ℝ} {t G ρ : ℝ}
    (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) (hG : 0 ≤ G)
    (hc : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ c i j)
    (hg : ∀ i j, |g i j| ≤ G) (hg' : ∀ i j, |g' i j| ≤ G)
    (σ τ : PartialMatching m n) (hσ : σ.card = min m n)
    (hσopt : σ.cost (fun i j ↦ c i j + t * g i j) =
      maxCardValue (fun i j ↦ c i j + t * g i j))
    (hτ : τ.card = min m n)
    (s : Finset (Fin m × Fin n)) (hsσ : s ⊆ σ.edges) (hsτ : s ⊆ τ.edges)
    (hrel : ∀ e ∈ s, c' e.1 e.2 ≤ (1 + ρ) * c e.1 e.2)
    (hprobe : ∀ e ∈ s, g' e.1 e.2 = g e.1 e.2) :
    maxCardValue (fun i j ↦ c' i j + t * g' i j) ≤
      (1 + ρ) * maxCardValue (fun i j ↦ c i j + t * g i j) +
        ρ * |t| * G * (min m n : ℝ) +
        (∑ e ∈ τ.edges \ s, c' e.1 e.2) +
        2 * |t| * G * ((min m n - s.card : ℕ) : ℝ)

d-e7e434bb5eb7dc7b05b65888.name: OTSelector.sq_dist_le_dyadic_partitionDistance
d-e7e434bb5eb7dc7b05b65888.declaration_documentation: The deterministic geometric input of the dyadic matching bound: on the unit cube, the squared Euclidean distance is bounded by the terminal dyadic cell diameter plus the geometric sum of dyadic cell mismatches. The terminal term is `4 q (1 / 4) ^ K`. At the first mismatching level `k₀`, the points still share a cell of the preceding level, which bounds the squared distance by `4 q (1 / 4) ^ k₀`; the mismatch at level `k₀` alone contributes `8 q (1 / 4) ^ k₀` to the weighted sum.
d-e7e434bb5eb7dc7b05b65888.name_identity_policy: Current explicit rename is applied when recorded; private/native names otherwise denote the immutable inspected source identity, with current source_name preserved.
d-e7e434bb5eb7dc7b05b65888.exact_source_header:
theorem sq_dist_le_dyadic_partitionDistance {q K : ℕ} (hK : 0 < K)
    {x y : Fin q → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i ∧ x i < 1) (hy : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i < 1) :
    ∑ i, (x i - y i)^2 ≤
      (4 * q : ℝ) * ((1/4 : ℝ) ^ K) +
        ∑ k ∈ Finset.range K, (8 * q : ℝ) * ((1/4 : ℝ) ^ k) *
          partitionDistance (dyadicCell q k x) (dyadicCell q k y)

    {M : Type*} [MeasurableSpace M] [MeasurableSingletonClass M] [PseudoMetricSpace M]
    [NeZero n] (X Y : Fin n → M) (φ : M → ℝ) (probe : M × M → ℝ)

    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (X Y : Fin n → M) (φ : M → ℝ) (probe : M × M → ℝ)

    perturbedAssignmentValue (fun i j ↦ k * distanceSlackEdgeCost X Y φ i j)
        (fun i j ↦ probe (X i, Y j)) 0 / (n : ℝ) =

theorem hierarchy_optimal_cost_bound
    {X : Type*} {K n : ℕ} {C : Fin K → Type*} [∀ k, Fintype (C k)]
    (cell : (k : Fin K) → X → C k)
    (hnested : ∀ (k l : Fin K), k ≤ l → ∀ a b,
      cell l a = cell l b → cell k a = cell k b)
    (x y : Fin n → X) {σ : Assignment n}
    (hσ : OptimalAssignment (hierarchyEdgeCost cell x y) σ)

theorem exists_partialMatching_hierarchy_cost_bound
    {X : Type*} {K a b : ℕ} {C : Fin K → Type*} [∀ k, Fintype (C k)]
    (cell : (k : Fin K) → X → C k)
    (hnested : ∀ (k l : Fin K), k ≤ l → ∀ x y : X,
      cell l x = cell l y → cell k x = cell k y)
    (x : Fin a → X) (y : Fin b → X)
    (cost : Fin a → Fin b → ℝ)
    (base : ℝ) (hb : 0 ≤ base) (weight : Fin K → ℝ) (hw : ∀ k, 0 ≤ weight k)
    (hcost : ∀ i j, cost i j ≤
      base + ∑ k, weight k * partitionDistance (cell k (x i)) (cell k (y j))) :
    ∃ σ : PartialMatching a b,
      σ.card = min a b ∧
      σ.cost cost ≤ (max a b : ℝ) * base +
        (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ∑ k, weight k *
          (∑ c, |partitionCount (cell k ∘ x) c - partitionCount (cell k ∘ y) c| +

      cell l x = cell l y → cell k x = cell k y)
    (x : Fin a → X) (y : Fin b → X)
    (cost : Fin a → Fin b → ℝ)
    (base : ℝ) (hb : 0 ≤ base) (weight : Fin K → ℝ) (hw : ∀ k, 0 ≤ weight k)
    (hcost : ∀ i j, cost i j ≤
      base + ∑ k, weight k * partitionDistance (cell k (x i)) (cell k (y j)))

d-ae63033f1ed7847b2ac6b917.declaration_documentation: Removing each block's actual signed excess from its unused original indices gives the local minimum count and equal remaining colors. This is a local statement; the complete original graph may have smaller global rank.

theorem originalBlockDeletedUnused_count_spec
    (σ : OTSelector.PartialMatching m n) (c : Fin m → B) (d : Fin n → B)
    (hsame : ∀ e ∈ σ.edges, c e.1 = d e.2) (b : B)
    (Ds : Finset (Fin m)) (Dt : Finset (Fin n))
    (hDs : Ds ⊆ σ.freeRows.filter (fun i ↦ c i = b))
    (hDt : Dt ⊆ σ.freeCols.filter (fun j ↦ d j = b))
    (hDscard : Ds.card = (Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ c i = b)).card -
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun j ↦ d j = b)).card)
    (hDtcard : Dt.card = (Finset.univ.filter (fun j ↦ d j = b)).card -
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ c i = b)).card) :
    let U := (σ.freeRows.filter (fun i ↦ c i = b)) \ Ds
    let V := (σ.freeCols.filter (fun j ↦ d j = b)) \ Dt
    U ⊆ σ.freeRows ∧ V ⊆ σ.freeCols ∧
      (∀ i ∈ U, c i = b) ∧ (∀ j ∈ V, d j = b) ∧
      (σ.edges.filter (fun e ↦ c e.1 = b)).card + U.card =
        min (Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ c i = b)).card
          (Finset.univ.filter (fun j ↦ d j = b)).card ∧ U.card = V.card

theorem exists_fine_good_bad_matching_union
    (sourceTag : Fin m → Option (CellRefinedType C T))
    (targetTag : Fin n → Option (CellRefinedType C T))
    (good bad : OTSelector.PartialMatching m n)
    (hg : ∀ e ∈ good.edges,

    (hb : ∀ e ∈ bad.edges,

      ∀ cost : Fin m → Fin n → ℝ, merged.cost cost = good.cost cost + bad.cost cost

theorem abs_free_cell_imbalance_le_original_add_crossings
    {C : Type*} [DecidableEq C] (σ : PartialMatching m n)
    (a : Fin m → C) (b : Fin n → C) (c : C) :
    |(∑ i ∈ σ.freeRows, if a i = c then (1 : ℝ) else 0) -
      (∑ j ∈ σ.freeCols, if b j = c then (1 : ℝ) else 0)| ≤
      |(∑ i, if a i = c then (1 : ℝ) else 0) -
        (∑ j, if b j = c then (1 : ℝ) else 0)| +
      ∑ e ∈ σ.edges,
        if (a e.1 = c ∧ b e.2 ≠ c) ∨ (a e.1 ≠ c ∧ b e.2 = c) then (1 : ℝ) else 0

theorem sum_abs_free_cell_imbalance_le_original_add_crossings
    {C : Type*} [Fintype C] [DecidableEq C] (σ : PartialMatching m n)
    (a : Fin m → C) (b : Fin n → C) :
    (∑ c, |(∑ i ∈ σ.freeRows, if a i = c then (1 : ℝ) else 0) -
      (∑ j ∈ σ.freeCols, if b j = c then (1 : ℝ) else 0)|) ≤
      (∑ c, |(∑ i, if a i = c then (1 : ℝ) else 0) -
        (∑ j, if b j = c then (1 : ℝ) else 0)|) +

d-6545748abc42da822c6fdc08.declaration_documentation: Actual signed excesses are deleted on one unchanged original index set. Its block restrictions therefore give both the exact local minimum completion count and equally many unused source/target labels, without a global rank premise.

theorem originalGlobalDeletedUnused_count_spec
    (σ : OTSelector.PartialMatching m n) (c : Fin m → B) (d : Fin n → B)
    (hsame : ∀ e ∈ σ.edges, c e.1 = d e.2)
    (Ds : Finset (Fin m)) (Dt : Finset (Fin n))
    (hDs : Ds ⊆ σ.freeRows) (hDt : Dt ⊆ σ.freeCols)
    (hDscard : ∀ b, (Ds.filter (fun i ↦ c i = b)).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ c i = b)).card - (Finset.univ.filter (fun j ↦ d j = b)).card)
    (hDtcard : ∀ b, (Dt.filter (fun j ↦ d j = b)).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun j ↦ d j = b)).card - (Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ c i = b)).card) :
    let U := σ.freeRows \ Ds
    let V := σ.freeCols \ Dt
    U ⊆ σ.freeRows ∧ V ⊆ σ.freeCols ∧
      ∀ b,
        (σ.edges.filter (fun e ↦ c e.1 = b)).card + (U.filter (fun i ↦ c i = b)).card =
          min (Finset.univ.filter (fun i ↦ c i = b)).card (Finset.univ.filter (fun j ↦ d j = b)).card ∧
        (U.filter (fun i ↦ c i = b)).card = (V.filter (fun j ↦ d j = b)).card

theorem unusedOriginalLaw_after_reserveDeletion
    {X I J : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] [Fintype I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq I] [DecidableEq J]
    (x : I → X) (reserve : J → X) (used : Finset I) (r : J ↪ I)
    (hpoints : ∀ j, x (r j) = reserve j)
    (hfree : Finset.univ.map r ⊆ Finset.univ \ used) (port : Measure X)
    (hwindow : (∑ i, Measure.dirac (x i)) =
      (∑ i ∈ used, Measure.dirac (x i)) + port + ∑ j, Measure.dirac (reserve j))
    (D : Finset J) :
    (∑ i ∈ (Finset.univ \ used) \ D.map r, Measure.dirac (x i)) =
      port + ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ \ D, Measure.dirac (reserve j)

d-a193a504d79a88cafb57eda9.name: OTSelector.maxCardValue_le_blockSum_add_repair
d-a193a504d79a88cafb57eda9.declaration_documentation: **Optimal block value plus hierarchical repair.** If `σ0` is the matching that is optimal in every leaf block, then the global optimal maximum-cardinality value is at most the sum of the leaf-block optimal values plus the telescoping repair sum. All edge costs are assumed nonnegative.

theorem maxCardValue_le_blockSum_add_repair
    {X : Type*} {K : ℕ} {C : ℕ → Type*}
    [∀ k, Fintype (C k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (C k)]
    (cell : (k : ℕ) → X → C k)
    (hnested : ∀ (k l : ℕ), k ≤ l → ∀ u v : X,
      cell l u = cell l v → cell k u = cell k v)
    {a b : ℕ} (x : Fin a → X) (y : Fin b → X)
    (cost : Fin a → Fin b → ℝ) (hnonneg : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ cost i j)
    (B : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hB : ∀ (k : ℕ), k < K → ∀ i j,
      cell k (x i) = cell k (y j) → cost i j ≤ B (k + 1))
    (hroot : ∀ u v : X, cell 0 u = cell 0 v) :
    PartialMatching.maxCardValue cost ≤
      (∑ c : C K,
        PartialMatching.maxCardValue
          (blockCost (fun i : Fin a => cell K (x i))
            (fun j : Fin b => cell K (y j)) cost c))
      + ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (K + 1), if 0 < k then
          B k * (1 / 2 : ℝ) *
            (cellDiscrepancy (cell k) x y - cellDiscrepancy (cell (k - 1)) x y)
        else 0

d-ae456a63956892bbac2f9df3.declaration_documentation: **Relative kinetic perturbation of the tilted value.** If the nonnegative kinetic matrix `c'` differs relatively by at most `delta <= 1` from `c`, and the probe is bounded by `G`, then the tilted least costs differ by at most `delta` times the tilted size plus the shift `|t| G` per matched pair.

theorem abs_maxCardValue_perturbed_sub_le_of_relative_kinetic
    {c c' g : Fin m → Fin n → ℝ} {t G δ : ℝ}
    (hδ0 : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ1 : δ ≤ 1) (hG0 : 0 ≤ G)
    (hc : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ c i j) (hg : ∀ i j, |g i j| ≤ G)
    (h : ∀ i j, |c' i j - c i j| ≤ δ * c i j) :
    |maxCardValue (fun i j => c' i j + t * g i j) -
        maxCardValue (fun i j => c i j + t * g i j)| ≤
      δ * (maxCardValue (fun i j => c i j + t * g i j) +
        (min m n : ℝ) * |t| * G)

d-cf50ea4f3750f2eed018ecf7.declaration_documentation: A legal reference matrix fixes a finite tolerance. Every actual original legal matrix whose full intensity-weighted class masses meet that tolerance produces the normalized retained/residual split needed for original population reconstruction. Actual and reference Hall are derived from their literal flows.

theorem exists_tolerance_normalized_reference_classSplit
    {M L : ℕ} (allowed : Fin M → Fin L → Prop)
    (horder : ∀ i i' j j', i ≤ i' → j' ≤ j → allowed i' j' → allowed i j)
    (a₀ : Fin M → ℝ) (b₀ : Fin L → ℝ) (P₀ : Fin M → Fin L → ℝ)
    (hP₀ : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ P₀ i j)
    (hrow₀ : ∀ i, ∑ j, P₀ i j = a₀ i) (hcol₀ : ∀ j, ∑ i, P₀ i j = b₀ j)
    (hzero₀ : ∀ i j, ¬ allowed i j → P₀ i j = 0)
    (d₀ η : ℝ) (hd₀ : 0 < d₀) (htotal₀ : ∑ i, a₀ i = d₀)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hη1 : η ≤ 1) :
    ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ (d ε : ℝ) (a : Fin M → ℝ) (b : Fin L → ℝ)
      (A : Fin M → Fin L → ℝ), 0 < d → 0 ≤ ε → d ≤ (1 + ε) * d₀ →
      (∀ i j, 0 ≤ A i j) →
      (∀ i, ∑ j, A i j = a i) → (∀ j, ∑ i, A i j = b j) →
      (∀ i j, ¬ allowed i j → A i j = 0) → (∑ i, a i = 1) →
      (∀ i, |d * a i - a₀ i| ≤ δ) → (∀ j, |d * b j - b₀ j| ≤ δ) →
      let Q := referenceResidualClockFlow a₀ b₀ η (fun i ↦ d * a i) (fun j ↦ d * b j)
      (∀ i j, 0 ≤ (1 - η) * P₀ i j / d) ∧
      (∀ i j, 0 ≤ Q i j / d) ∧
      (∀ i, ∑ j, ((1 - η) * P₀ i j / d + Q i j / d) = a i) ∧
      (∀ j, ∑ i, ((1 - η) * P₀ i j / d + Q i j / d) = b j) ∧
      (∀ i j, ¬ allowed i j → (1 - η) * P₀ i j / d = 0 ∧ Q i j / d = 0) ∧
      (∑ i, ∑ j, Q i j / d) ≤ η + ε

theorem exists_ordered_legal_clockBin_graph
    {m n : ℕ} (S : Fin m → Set ℝ) (T : Fin n → Set ℝ)
    (hSbound : ∀ i, BddAbove (S i)) (hTbound : ∀ j, BddBelow (T j))
    (gap : ℝ) (hgap : 0 < gap)
    (hSdiam : ∀ i, ∀ x ∈ S i, ∀ y ∈ S i, |x - y| ≤ gap / 4)
    (hTdiam : ∀ j, ∀ x ∈ T j, ∀ y ∈ T j, |x - y| ≤ gap / 4) :
    ∃ (e : Fin m ≃ Fin m) (f : Fin n ≃ Fin n),
      let allowed := fun i j ↦ sSup (S (e i)) + gap / 2 ≤ sInf (T (f j))
      (∀ i i' j j', i ≤ i' → j' ≤ j → allowed i' j' → allowed i j) ∧
      (∀ i j, ∀ s ∈ S (e i), ∀ t ∈ T (f j), gap ≤ t - s → allowed i j) ∧
      (∀ i j, allowed i j → ∀ s ∈ S (e i), ∀ t ∈ T (f j), s ≤ t)

theorem exists_finite_reference_classSplit_tolerances
    {C : Type*} [Fintype C] {M L : ℕ}
    (allowed : Fin M → Fin L → Prop)
    (horder : ∀ i i' j j', i ≤ i' → j' ≤ j → allowed i' j' → allowed i j)
    (a₀ : C → Fin M → ℝ) (b₀ : C → Fin L → ℝ)
    (P₀ : C → Fin M → Fin L → ℝ) (d₀ : C → ℝ)
    (hP₀ : ∀ c i j, 0 ≤ P₀ c i j)
    (hrow₀ : ∀ c i, ∑ j, P₀ c i j = a₀ c i) (hcol₀ : ∀ c j, ∑ i, P₀ c i j = b₀ c j)
    (hzero₀ : ∀ c i j, ¬ allowed i j → P₀ c i j = 0)
    (hd₀ : ∀ c, 0 < d₀ c) (htotal₀ : ∀ c, ∑ i, a₀ c i = d₀ c)
    (η : ℝ) (hη : 0 < η) (hη1 : η ≤ 1) :
    ∃ δ : C → ℝ, (∀ c, 0 < δ c) ∧
      ∀ (c : C) (d ε : ℝ) (a : Fin M → ℝ) (b : Fin L → ℝ) (A : Fin M → Fin L → ℝ),
        0 < d → 0 ≤ ε → d ≤ (1 + ε) * d₀ c →
        (∀ i j, 0 ≤ A i j) → (∀ i, ∑ j, A i j = a i) → (∀ j, ∑ i, A i j = b j) →
        (∀ i j, ¬ allowed i j → A i j = 0) → (∑ i, a i = 1) →
        (∀ i, |d * a i - a₀ c i| ≤ δ c) → (∀ j, |d * b j - b₀ c j| ≤ δ c) →
        let Q := referenceResidualClockFlow (a₀ c) (b₀ c) η (fun i ↦ d * a i) (fun j ↦ d * b j)
        (∀ i j, 0 ≤ (1 - η) * P₀ c i j / d) ∧
        (∀ i j, 0 ≤ Q i j / d) ∧
        (∀ i, ∑ j, ((1 - η) * P₀ c i j / d + Q i j / d) = a i) ∧
        (∀ j, ∑ i, ((1 - η) * P₀ c i j / d + Q i j / d) = b j) ∧
        (∀ i j, ¬ allowed i j → (1 - η) * P₀ c i j / d = 0 ∧ Q i j / d = 0) ∧
        (∑ i, ∑ j, Q i j / d) ≤ η + ε

theorem exists_tolerance_reference_residual_hall
    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J]
    (neighbor : Finset I → Finset J) (a₀ : I → ℝ) (b₀ : J → ℝ)
    (ha₀ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ a₀ i) (hb₀ : ∀ j, 0 ≤ b₀ j)
    (hhall₀ : ∀ A, 0 ≤ referenceHallSlack neighbor a₀ b₀ A)
    {η : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) :
    ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ (a : I → ℝ) (b : J → ℝ),
      (∀ i, 0 ≤ a i) → (∀ j, 0 ≤ b j) →
      (∀ A, 0 ≤ referenceHallSlack neighbor a b A) →
      (∀ i, |a i - a₀ i| ≤ δ) → (∀ j, |b j - b₀ j| ≤ δ) →
      (∀ i, 0 ≤ a i - (1 - η) * a₀ i) ∧
      (∀ j, 0 ≤ b j - (1 - η) * b₀ j) ∧
      ∀ A, 0 ≤ referenceHallSlack neighbor
        (fun i ↦ a i - (1 - η) * a₀ i) (fun j ↦ b j - (1 - η) * b₀ j) A

    (r : α → ℕ) (htotal : ∑ j, r j = n + 1) (hr : ∀ j, 0 < r j)
    (cost : Fin (n + 1) → α → ℝ) (i₀ : Fin (n + 1)) (root : α)
    (a : Fin n → α)

      (fun k l ↦ cost (i₀.succAbove k) l) a)

theorem exists_optimalCapacityAssignment_reroot_terminal_row
    (r : α → ℕ) (htotal : ∑ j, r j = n + 1) (hr : ∀ j, 0 < r j)
    (cost : Fin (n + 1) → α → ℝ) (i₀ : Fin (n + 1)) (root : α)
    (a : Fin n → α)
    (ha : OptimalCapacityAssignment (capacityDeficit r root)
      (fun s j ↦ cost (i₀.succAbove s) j) a)
    (hunique : ∀ b, OptimalCapacityAssignment (capacityDeficit r root)
      (fun s j ↦ cost (i₀.succAbove s) j) b → b = a)
    (k : Fin n) (u : α) (hu : u ≠ a k)
    (htight : capacityVacancyRowPotential r htotal hr cost i₀ (i₀.succAbove k) -
      capacityVacancyPrice r htotal cost i₀ u (hr u) = cost (i₀.succAbove k) u) :
    ∃ b, OptimalCapacityAssignment (capacityDeficit r (a k))
        (fun s j ↦ cost (i₀.succAbove s) j) b ∧ b k = u ∧
      ∀ s, a s = a k → s ≠ k → b s = a s
